findings.title: The PEMS07 Avg row is inconsistent with its four component values
findings.detail: In v2 Table 10, the four TimesCLIP MSE values average 0.08975, but the table reports 0.358. The MAE values average 0.193, but the table reports 0.773. This supports an aggregation or labeling error, not a finding that the experimental data were fabricated.

evidence.scope: arXiv 2506.24124v2, Table 10 (PEMS07; horizons 12, 24, 48, 96) and Table 2.
evidence.observation: The four TimesCLIP MSE values are 0.063, 0.074, 0.106, 0.116: (0.063 + 0.074 + 0.106 + 0.116) / 4 = 0.08975, versus reported Avg 0.358. The MAE values 0.175, 0.183, 0.204, 0.210 average 0.193, versus reported Avg 0.773. The reported averages even exceed every component in their respective columns. Table 2 reuses these aggregates.
evidence.reason: An average with nonnegative weights cannot exceed all its components. Rounding cannot reconcile these values. The table therefore contains an aggregation or labeling error affecting the interpretation of the reported absolute errors.
evidence.limitation: The aggregate values are close to sums rather than means; other methods show a similar pattern. A shared scaling error could leave the within-dataset ranking unchanged. The table inconsistency does not demonstrate that the component results were invented.

findings.title: Padding exclusion can exhaust valid tokens and repeatedly select a masked token
findings.detail: The selector caps its token budget by the total token count, without subtracting excluded padding tokens. When valid candidates run out, the remaining iterations take argmax over all-negative-infinity scores and repeatedly select index 0.

evidence.scope: MMTok commit 8e2686836ed5bbe05d064f1d1c20e50c73c70b94; LLaVA-1.5 tensor-input path with padding exclusion, finite coverage scores and a requested budget exceeding eligible candidates.
evidence.observation: The selector caps its token budget by the total token count, without subtracting excluded padding tokens. When valid candidates run out, the remaining iterations take argmax over all-negative-infinity scores and repeatedly select index 0.
evidence.reason: For a 1008-by-336 image, the published padding rule excludes eight rows at the top and eight at the bottom of a 24-by-24 grid, leaving 192 eligible tokens. With the README budget of 256 and padding exclusion enabled, the first 192 iterations consume all eligible tokens; the next 64 select masked index 0. The output is neither padding-free nor a subset of 256 distinct tokens.
evidence.limitation: The result follows from the padding arithmetic and loop control flow. The frequency of this input condition in the paper benchmarks was not measured.

findings.title: The equation and public code use opposite update signs
findings.detail: AAAI 2026 Equation (2) adds the gradient, while the pinned code subtracts it. The equation and released code specify opposite update directions. This discrepancy is not evidence of data fabrication.

evidence.scope: AAAI 2026 publication, Equation (2), PDF page 4 / printed page 33695; Lateng-Reasoning commit 94e70c46acb39c45c713d010d53f9e06421527d8.
evidence.observation: Equation (2) specifies h_new = h + eta * gradient[L], where L = MSE(h_good, h) - MSE(h_bad, h). The released coconut_search.py computes that loss but updates h by subtracting learning_rate * gradient[L].
evidence.reason: For positive step sizes the displayed equation and code move in opposite directions on the same objective. A reader implementing the stated method would not reproduce the released update rule.
evidence.limitation: This identifies a paper/code specification mismatch; it does not establish which rule generated the reported results. The code refines embeddings without updating model parameters. No fabrication or individual intent is inferred.

findings.title: Shape-encoder validation reuses the first five training objects
findings.detail: The public VQ-VAE entry point builds train and val from the same dataset root. The loader builds the same eligible model list for both and truncates non-training splits to its first five entries. Validation IoU is then used to select the best checkpoint.

evidence.scope: RoomDesigner commit 3980e06bfc48f76f3f1efb2d2182c0c871d2231b: 3DILG/run_vqvae.py, datasets.py and FRONT.py.
evidence.observation: The public VQ-VAE entry point builds train and val from the same dataset root. The loader builds the same eligible model list for both and truncates non-training splits to its first five entries. Validation IoU is then used to select the best checkpoint.
evidence.reason: The validation objects are a prefix of the training object list, not a disjoint object split. Resampling surface and occupancy points on these objects does not create validation on unseen object identities. The checkpoint selection consequently measures reconstruction on objects already included in training.
evidence.limitation: This is the public shape-encoder training path, separate from the room-level scene-generation test split and its reported FID/SCA results.

evidence.reason: For two frames with similarity rows [-a,-a] and [a,a], a>0, the upper-triangular transition matrix and uniform prior produce initial scores [-a/2,-a/2]. The second-frame scores are [0,-a²/4]; backtracking returns [1,0]. This contradicts the temporal-order constraint in Section 3.4.
evidence.limitation: The counterexample is derived from the Viterbi option. The default command-line option is sorting.

findings.title: A final rejection can associate media with an unexecuted revised prompt
findings.detail: After a rejected attempt, both the keyframe and clip loops update the prompt even on the last permitted attempt. The pipeline then saves that revised prompt together with the media generated before the revision.

evidence.scope: arXiv 2609.07720v1; CineCrew commit 9a00efa7db65ba028c1523907f6cee844776123a
evidence.observation: After a rejected attempt, both the keyframe and clip loops update the prompt even on the last permitted attempt. The pipeline then saves that revised prompt together with the media generated before the revision.
evidence.reason: With max_retries=0, prompt P0 produces image I0; rejection supplies P1; the saved image remains I0 while the final prompt becomes P1. The same mismatch occurs when the last attempt of a longer retry loop is rejected. Final FilmDSL and VideoJob fields can therefore misstate the generation conditions.
evidence.limitation: The path requires a final rejected attempt with a nonempty revised_prompt; it is established by static control-flow analysis.

findings.title: RepCount combined statistics conflict with the reported subsets
findings.detail: Table 1 gives 1,041 Part-A videos with mean count 14.99 and 410 Part-B videos with mean count 9.27, but reports a combined mean of 15.932. The combined duration mean also differs from the sample-size-weighted subset means.

evidence.scope: arXiv 2204.01018v1, Table 1 and Section 3, checked in the arXiv HTML
evidence.observation: Table 1 gives 1,041 Part-A videos with mean count 14.99 and 410 Part-B videos with mean count 9.27, but reports a combined mean of 15.932. The combined duration mean also differs from the sample-size-weighted subset means.
evidence.reason: The count mean must lie between the two subset means; the reported sizes give approximately 13.374, not 15.932. Duration means 30.67 and 28.53 seconds give approximately 30.065 seconds, not the table value 29.359. Section 3 additionally states 39.359 seconds. Two-decimal rounding cannot explain the discrepancies.
evidence.limitation: The arithmetic checks the printed summary statistics; raw video annotations were not recomputed.

findings.title: The postfix search-space claim confuses token vocabulary with complete sequences
findings.detail: Appendix A attributes a reduction from an exponential search space to |C| = |O| + |X|D + 3 to postfix notation. The expression adds operator, feature and special-token counts; it does not count complete transformation sequences.

evidence.scope: arXiv 2506.09085v1, Appendix A and Figure 7; the counterexample respects the prompt limit on the number of feature combinations.
evidence.observation: Appendix A attributes a reduction from an exponential search space to |C| = |O| + |X|D + 3 to postfix notation. The expression adds operator, feature and special-token counts; it does not count complete transformation sequences.
evidence.reason: Even under the prompt in Figure 7, take k distinct features with k below 50 and select either sin or tanh for each. This gives 2^k valid feature sets while the token vocabulary stays fixed for those features. Infix-to-postfix conversion also preserves each represented expression. Removing brackets therefore does not establish the claimed sequence-space bound.
evidence.limitation: The reviewed manuscript is arXiv 2506.09085v1.
